rows: Quarter to golf ball-size hail reported in Huckabay and Morgan Mill.
Reported between Bluff Dale and Chalk Mountain.
Several residents reported seeing a tornado near Alexander. A local dairy was destroyed, as was a barn. Damage to fences and trees was also reported. Numerous cows were killed.

Many local residents saw a tornado touch down south of Stephenville. The tornado apparently caused minor damage to trees and fences before lifting off just north of town. Minor damage was also reported at a cement plant on the eastern edge of town.
A tornado was reported on the ground at Highway 377 North moving north towards CR 176. No damage was reported.
Brief tornado near Thurber. No damage reported.
A limb fell on a car, and a power pole was blown down.
A roof was blown off a house and a tree fell on a car in Stephenville.
A large tree was blown onto a house in extreme northeast Erath County.

Golfball to baseball-size hail fell south of Gordon on Interstate-20.

A damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service in Fort Worth found that a tornado formed near the intersection of CR 120 and CR 125. The tornado moved east causing damage to a shed and a mobile home. Tree limbs were damaged across CR 118. This tornado was rated an EF-0…

Trees and large limbs were blown down and roof shingles were torn off roofs.
A storm spotter saw a tornado touchdown about 2.5 miles south of Dublin on CR 338. The tornado remained on the ground for 22 seconds and no damage was reported.

The media relayed that numerous large limbs were blown down in town.

Numerous large trees and tree branches were knocked down across Stephenville by thunderstorm winds. The newspaper reported that the northwest parts of the city appeared to be hit the hardest by the winds. Power lines were also down in parts of the city.

The Dublin Police Department reported damage from a tornado early in the morning of March 9th. The tornado was short lived, and produced minor damage to approximately ten buildings in downtown Dublin.
